review.finding: restore_tracked_log promises it never raises for an expected condition, because an exception strands a half-created worktree. Every I/O is guarded EXCEPT _classify_salvage, whose read_text_verbatim is unprotected. On Windows a handle on the just-renamed file surfaces as PermissionError, which propagates through commit_main_tracked_drift and sweep_outbox_to_branch (both also never-raises) into setup_iterate_worktree step 5 AFTER git worktree add succeeded — and by then the log has been renamed aside and recreated from HEAD, so the salvage is orphaned with no reason naming it.
review.resolution: FIXED — wrapped in try/except OSError, returning main_tracked_salvage_unclassified which names the salvage file.

review.finding: Both os.replace calls are bare, with no retry past a Windows sharing violation, in the module whose stated threat model IS the WebUI writer. Failure is safe but persistent: a holder that reappears each sweep yields main_tracked_salvage_rename_failed forever. Linux CI can never surface it.
review.resolution: FIXED for the rename-aside via the newly public atomic_write.replace_retrying. DELIBERATELY NOT applied to the put-back after the doubt review showed retrying there inverts the safety argument.

review.finding: On three return paths the salvage is the ONLY copy of the preserved data, and it is gitignored — a file git clean -x deletes. That is precisely the hazard sweep_drift and sweep_outbox refuse for the outbox; the module docstring presented the gitignoring purely as an upside.
review.resolution: FIXED (documentation) — the trade-off is now stated where the salvage is created, and the doubt review's follow-up made plan_main_tracked_drift repeat the pointer on every later refusal.

review.finding: adopt_note is captured but discarded on every post-adoption error return (add_failed, git_timeout, commit_timeout, commit_failed), so the only pointer to the sole surviving copy of salvaged lines never reaches a human.
review.resolution: FIXED — with_adopt_note() in lib/sweep_result.py, applied at all four; also fixes the no_branch_change swallow.

review.finding: The new ReconcileResult.warnings never reach a human on the default output path — only --json emits them. The invalid branch is the worst case and is newly reachable via the finding-25 change.
review.resolution: FIXED — warnings printed to stderr on every status.

review.finding: --apply --commit evaluates its main-tree guards AFTER the destructive rewrite. On a detached HEAD, inside a rebase, or with anything staged, --commit leaves the operator with exactly the divergence the flag exists to prevent. reconcile_main_triage checks all three BEFORE it mutates. The tests assert post-rewrite behaviour and would keep passing under the correct ordering, so they do not defend it.
review.resolution: FIXED — commit_preflight() runs before apply_gc_reporting; returns rc 2 with nothing rewritten. Tests rewritten to assert the log is byte-unchanged.

review.finding: path_matches_head collapses 'git could not answer' into 'dirty'. Fail-closed for the --commit precondition but fail-LOUD for the warning: a non-git directory printed the full 'deliver NOTHING' text. The inverse bites AC-1: on a timeout it returned None and --apply printed nothing at all.
review.resolution: FIXED — tri-state, then a fourth state (not_a_repo) after the doubt review.

review.finding: 'Last look before we publish' is followed by durable_atomic_write, which fsyncs before its os.replace — the slowest call in the function — so the residual window is materially larger than the wording implies. Secondary: the .bak is published BEFORE the fingerprint check, so a refusal leaves a .bak for a compaction that never happened, and the RuntimeError escapes main() as a traceback.
review.resolution: FIXED — residual named; backup fsynced before the compare and published by a rename after it (revised again by the doubt review); main() catches RuntimeError.

review.finding: main_tracked_late_append_salvaged formats the FRESH count, which is 0 on an idempotent replay — so the operator reads '0 append(s) recovered' on a path that did preserve something.
review.resolution: FIXED — reports observed and newly-buffered counts separately.

review.finding: triage_gc_core.py is a brand-new file at exactly 300 lines — zero headroom, created by a change justifying each extraction as one that 'gives both headroom'. sweep_outbox.py went from 296 to 300.
review.resolution: FIXED — duplicated rationale shed from triage_gc_core; with_adopt_note relocated to sweep_result, leaving sweep_outbox at 298.

review.finding: --commit without --apply is silently ignored: main() returns before the commit block. Exit 0, no note.
--project-root is treated as the main tree while every docstring says MAIN. Run from an iterate worktree, --commit would land the compaction commit on the iterate branch.
review.resolution: FIXED — --commit refuses outside the main root. (The first attempt resolved main for the git half only, which was incoherent; a new test caught it.)

review.finding: The main_tracked_ branch comment still says 'No loss — the drift is buffered and the next sweep completes it', now false for three new salvage reasons printed under that banner.
review.resolution: FIXED — the salvage class is called out as not self-healing.

review.finding: The central assertion of the cross_component test is hedged with an `or`; the mechanism produces exactly skipped + main_tracked_diverged. Line 93's `in (no_drift, adoptable)` has the same problem in reverse — adoptable would mean the commit did NOT clean the log.
Two monkeypatches discriminate on a hardcoded '.salvage-' substring, so renaming the naming scheme silently turns both into no-ops that still pass green — a self-disarming test.
review.resolution: FIXED — both key on the claimed path object and assert a `fired` tripwire.

notes: Verified sound and NOT changed: no cycles (the isolated-subprocess import smoke test is the right instrument); no name drift in the re-exports; rollback_failed_commit cannot escape its contract.
Unasserted behaviour change surfaced: apply_gc used to publish via open(tmp,'w') (CRLF on Windows) and now always writes LF. An improvement, but nothing pinned it — a test was added.

Trust ranking given with no mutation evidence for three of four fixes: f25 and f16b trusted; f23 trusted for the mechanism not the envelope; f16a explicitly NOT trusted, which is what led to findings 6, 7 and 11.
